guidance: A field check of a balanced ventilation core from four duct temperatures, not a certified rating. Measure steady-state dry-bulb readings at the normal fan speed and not during a defrost cycle; the page reports sensible effectiveness only and assumes balanced supply and exhaust airflow.
method: The page applies the sensible-effectiveness equation of AHRI Standard 1060 (I-P) 2018, Appendix C Equation C1, with the station numbers of its Figure 1: effectiveness is the capacity rate at station 2 times the supply-air temperature change from the outdoor air, divided by the minimum capacity rate times the difference between the return air at station 3 and the outdoor air at station 1. At balanced supply and exhaust airflow the two capacity rates are equal, so the ratio is one and the arithmetic reduces to (supply - outdoor) / (return - outdoor); with unbalanced airflow the mass-flow ratio has to be applied and this page does not do that. Only dry-bulb temperature is used, so the result is sensible effectiveness: an ERV's latent and total effectiveness need humidity ratios and are not modelled. The air leaving the exhaust side is used only as a balance check, because at balanced airflow the supply should gain the heat the exhaust loses. The comparison band borrows the published-rating allowance of AHRI 1060 section 5.1.1: a measured value may sit up to four relative percentage points plus one absolute point below the rating, or two points, whichever is larger, so a 75% rating has a 71% floor. A field reading with hand-held probes is not a conforming ASHRAE 84 rating test, so a result under the band is a reason to repeat the measurement, not proof that the core is faulty. The recovered load is 1.08 x CFM x temperature change, where 1.08 is 60 minutes x 0.075 lb/ft3 x 0.24 Btu/lb-F for standard air at sea level. Readings whose outdoor-to-return spread is under five degrees are refused because the ratio has no meaning there, and a spread under ten degrees is flagged because a one-degree probe error moves the answer by several points. Everything runs in the browser with no uploads, storage or network access.
